title: HPSM-POC: telemetry stopped at round 3 (NO GO). Leave it stopped?
bluf: No action needed unless you want telemetry restarted. The round-3 gate (B447) returned NO GO, so by your rule telemetry (HPSMPOC-224) stops here: nothing was merged, deployed or sent, and the branch b429/telemetry-224 stays unmerged. Round 3 fixed what you asked: exception records are closed on both apps, and no connection string can stop either app. Still open, 7 findings of Major or worse (copied from the gate's findings list): Blockers B447-1 (the API's request row carries a runtime-built exception type name), B447-2 (a span event's name leaves as a log message), B447-3 (a log category built at run time leaves verbatim), B447-9 (for 13 malformed connection strings the Azure exporter writes the string to its own diagnostics log); Majors B447-4 (the web keeps some span names by shape), B447-5 (the README states the opposite of B447-1/-2), B447-10 (one start-up guard mutant survives every test). No product code builds such names today, but any library that does would leak them. Disclosure: one early test run by the gate was not network-fenced and may have sent scrubbed test telemetry under a made-up key to a Microsoft Application Insights host (no credential, no customer or personal data); every later run was fenced.

default_action: Telemetry stays stopped and nothing is deployed. Tuesday has the HPSM-POC records seat write the gate's findings onto HPSMPOC-224 (facts only) and keeps the branch unmerged.
_override_prior: Different decision: the prior Datasec rulings on this subject approved turning telemetry on and allowed one more fix round; that round has now come back NO GO, so this card asks only whether it stays stopped (measured: B447 STATUS last line, 14:5x).
